thin_core.rule: admit only machine-consequential accepted clauses needed by competency questions; keep detailed semantics in natural domain contracts; add J2 coverage and J3 predicates later

structural_burden.burden_finding: RICH_ACCEPTED requires a broader mandatory J1 review surface unless later-owned fields are made optional/deferred. Making those fields selective/deferred causes the design to converge toward THIN_ACCEPTED's J1/J2/J3 allocation.

control_power.thin: All 37 admitted CQs remain answerable through accepted clauses, domain-native contracts, generated control objects, natural-owner runtime facts and executable predicates.
control_power.rich: Can also support the same control when embedded in the same broader Project system.
control_power.rich_unique: No currently admitted CQ requires the richer unit fields as a second authoritative copy.

key_findings: Owner acceptance removes the original inference-authority/reproducibility objection for RICH_ACCEPTED.
Owner acceptance does not make birth-time unit grouping canonical when realization is naturally many-to-many or only known later.
Owner acceptance does not make J2 realization/evidence facts naturally knowable at J1.
A global realization-state enum is better treated as a derived view over source facts than as independent governing truth.
Rich fields with demonstrated value survive selectively in natural owners or as clause slots; they do not require the full rich unit model.
No current admitted competency question demonstrates unique required capability from the full RICH_ACCEPTED core.
